REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE BiVAHENG PINOY DILG Legal Opinion No. 28 s. 2012 APR 1 1 2012 'EPARTMENT ATTY. BAI ISRAHÄYDÄ SINSUÄT-BÄLÄMO Chief Legal Counsel Regional Legislative Assembly Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao Cotabato City Dear Atty. Balamo: This pertains to your letter seeking this Department's opinion regarding the claim of former Regional Legislative Assembly Speaker Rejie Sahali-CeneraIe to return to his office as Speaker of Regional Legislative Assembly. Per your letter former RLA Speaker Rejie Sahali-GeneraIe succeeded to the office of the Regional Vice Governor of the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao after former Regional Vice Governor Ansaruddin Alonto-Adiong succeeded to the Office of the Regional Governor due to the temporary legal incapacity of then Regional Governor Datu Zaldy Uy Ampatuan who was incarcerated for his alleged involvement in the 2009 Maguindanao Massacre. However, former Acting Regional Vice-Governor Generale is now asserting her right to return to her former office as speaker of Regional Legislative Assembly. Hence you referred the same for this Department's opinion. In your legal opinion dated January 20, 2012, you opined that "Acting Regional Vice-Governor (ARVG) Rejie S. Generale cannot anymore go back to her former office as Speaker of the Regional Assembly. Thus. it follows that she is NOT entitled to her salary and other emoluments attached to her former position. Neither can she return to the Assembly as a regular member thereof for the simple reason that her term of office as the elected representative of the Province of Tawi-Tawi has already expired last September 30. 2011." In reply thereto, please be informed that we concur with your opinion. While it is true that under Section 2 of Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 277 provides that "when the temporary vacancy ends and the incumbent Regional Vice Governor returns the Speaker of the Regional Assembly shall also ipso facto reassume his office as speaker", the aforequoted provision is applicable only if Ms. Generale's term of office as speaker or regular member of Regional Legislative Assembly has not yet expired. Ms. Generale's term of office has already expired on September 30, 2011, as elected representative of Tawi-Tawi, which under Section 4 of Republic Act No. 9054, is three years. Such being the case, Ms. Rejie Generale has no right to claim the said office since her term of office has already expired.

-2- Further, Republic Act No. 10153 otherwise known as "An Act Providing for the Synchronization of the Elections in the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) with the National and Local Elections and for Other Purposes," does not provide a provision which allow the Members of the Regional Legislative Assembly to extend their term of office. In fact Section 3 of RA 10153 provides that "The President shall appoint officer-in-charge for the Office of the Regional Governor, Regional Vice Governor and Members of the Regional Legislative Assembly who shall perform the functions pertaining to the said office until the officials duly elected in the May 2012 shall have qualified and assumed office." Hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, ESUS DOQ Director III 1.s:94/11
